summary: Interpreted the interface-probe receipt: all four comparisons resolve, and the two decisive ones show that an FSM implementing both BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore recorded 0 StoreConfiguration calls and 6 ApplyBatch configuration entries after a committed configuration change, while the ConfigurationStore-only control recorded 6 and 0. The source gives the mechanism — runFSM computes batchingEnabled once and then routes every batch through applyBatch, which forwards LogConfiguration entries to ApplyBatch and never calls StoreConfiguration, while StoreConfiguration is only reached from applySingle — so the callback ConfigurationStore documents unconditionally is not kept for that combination. I recorded it as a fourth asserted defect with its scope stated plainly: the same entries do reach ApplyBatch, which BatchingFSM documents as receiving them, so an application handling both paths loses nothing observable; what fails is the callback on which the interface's stated purpose (a persistent FSM state complete enough to recover without an external snapshot) depends. A Fact was added with the receipt indices and conditions, and the interpretation carries counterevidence (delivery via ApplyBatch, the unusual-but-allowed combination, the single measured trigger) and limitations (shared recorder, one execution, consequence argued from the documented purpose). No execution requested; about twenty-eight minutes of run time remain if a further lead is worth taking.
